reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides an instructional tutorial on creating a Google account, setting up a YouTube or Brand Account, creating a channel, and enabling features through phone verification. Its channel-growth and affiliate promotions are described as ordinary, while the external subscriber and earnings challenge is presented as separate and unverified rather than as part of the tutorial.

citations.quote: How to Create a YouTube Channel for Beginners (Step-by-Step Tutorial)
I'm going to walk you through step by step on how to do that.
In the YouTube Studio, we're going to go to this bottom-left corner, and we're going to go into the settings.
all you need to do this is to verify a phone number
put in that six digit number into Google

opening.argument: The solicitation is not merely about learning YouTube. It pairs a concrete outcome, “Your First 1K Subs” and “Your First $1K,” with an instruction to go to an external destination for a “FREE Challenge.” That is a low-barrier reward and income promise attached to viewer action. The tutorial supplies a credible-looking setting for the pitch, but the promised subscribers and money are not established by the account-creation steps themselves. A careful judge should treat the reward-linked external funnel as the central risk, rather than assuming that a free label makes the offer benign.

citations.quote: :fire: Get Your First 1K Subs & Earn Your First $1K on YouTube with this FREE Challenge here!
https://geni.us/8QBd

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional material does not neutralize the separate solicitation. The description explicitly connects the promised subscribers and earnings to a challenge and directs viewers outward, while the video also directs viewers toward classes, coaching, and other commercial offerings. Calling the challenge “separate” describes its placement, not whether it is a reward-linked acquisition funnel.

citations.quote: FREE Challenge here!
COURSES/ COACHING / MASTERMINDS: Learn about our online courses and in person events

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted challenge does not show that viewers must pay, deposit, surrender funds, or complete a deceptive verification flow. The actual demonstrated actions are ordinary account setup and phone verification, and the description identifies affiliate links rather than concealing them. A promise attached to a free educational challenge is insufficient by itself to establish scam conduct.

citations.quote: I'm going to walk you through step by step on how to do that.
all you need to do this is to verify a phone number
Some product links are affiliate links which means if you buy something we'll receive a small commission.

opening.argument: Several warning signals appear together: a large, specific monetary outcome, a large subscriber outcome, urgency-style promotional symbols, and a direct external link. The offer says viewers can get their first $1K and first 1K subscribers through a free challenge, then points them to a destination outside YouTube. Even without inventing hidden payment terms, that combination is materially more than neutral education: it is a high-return acquisition pitch whose conditions are not shown in the supplied material.

citations.quote: :fire: Get Your First 1K Subs & Earn Your First $1K on YouTube with this FREE Challenge here!
https://geni.us/8QBd
Start & Grow a High Profit & High Impact YouTube Channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account focuses on the screen demonstrations but leaves the strongest red flags unaddressed: the unusually concrete $1K outcome, the matching subscriber figure, and the external destination. The fact that the tutorial also shows Google menus does not explain why a beginner tutorial is paired with a high-profit challenge and multiple commercial calls to action.

citations.quote: Earn Your First $1K on YouTube
High Profit & High Impact YouTube Channel
FREE CLASS: Watch our FREE YouTube class here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are promotional signals, but they do not establish a scam category without a demonstrated payment, investment, or deceptive claim mechanism. The supplied tutorial actually shows account creation, channel creation, and feature setup. The description also expressly says the video is not sponsored and discloses affiliate commissions, which weighs against treating every external link as concealed fraud.

citations.quote: This video is NOT sponsored.
Some product links are affiliate links which means if you buy something we'll receive a small commission.
at this point, you have a YouTube channel

opening.argument: The ordinary tutorial framing functions as promotion because it moves viewers from a practical beginner lesson into a broader growth-and-income funnel. The description advertises a challenge promising subscribers and money, a high-profit masterclass, a book, a conference, and courses or coaching. That commercial ecosystem changes how the instructional material should be read: the account setup is useful onboarding, while the prominent payoff language steers viewers toward participation in an external offer.

citations.quote: Get Your First 1K Subs & Earn Your First $1K on YouTube with this FREE Challenge here!
Learn How to Start & Grow a High Profit & High Impact YouTube Channel with our FREE 1-Hour Masterclass HERE
COURSES/ COACHING / MASTERMINDS

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats the presence of genuine instructions as dispositive, but it does not account for the surrounding promotion. The description does not stop at account setup: it offers a challenge, masterclass, book, conference, and coaching contacts. That breadth supports reading the tutorial as an entry point into participation, not as an isolated operational demonstration.

citations.quote: Here are the ways to work with us here at Think Media:
BOOK: Check out the #1 best selling book YouTube Secrets here
CONFERENCE: Join us for the #1 video marketing conference in the US

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion around an educational video does not prove that the demonstrated tutorial is a scam. The actual narration explains how to create a channel and enable features, while the separate offers are labeled as free classes, affiliate links, books, or coaching. The quoted material shows marketing, but not a required payment or a false mechanism for obtaining the promised outcomes.
